Operator:  
Good morning, and welcome to the Vitality Consumer Goods Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. Instructions for queuing up will be given at that time. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Thompson, Vice President of Investor Relations.

Sarah Thompson:  
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Vitality Consumer Goods' Q3 2024 results. With me on the call are Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer; Jordan Lee, Chief Financial Officer; Taylor Kim, Chief Marketing Officer; and Morgan Patel, Chief Supply Chain Officer; and other members of our leadership team.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we will be making today are forward-looking and are based on our current expectations and beliefs. These statements are subject to certain risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed description of these risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera.

Alex Rivera:  
Thank you, Sarah. Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us. Vitality Consumer Goods delivered a solid Q3, demonstrating the resilience of our brands and the strength of our team. We are navigating a dynamic environment and remain focused on executing our strategic priorities.

Our discussion today will cover six key aspects: our overall company performance highlights, market share trends by category and region, key strategic priorities and progress, the decomposition of our organic sales growth into volume, price, and mix, our capital expenditure plans and priorities, and our gross margin guidance and key assumptions.

As we review these results, I'm proud to highlight the meaningful progress we've made against our four core strategic priorities: portfolio optimization, innovation and premiumization, sustainability leadership, and digital acceleration. These are tailored to handle headwinds like ongoing inflation, private label pressure, and consumers shifting toward health, wellness, and value. We've executed with discipline, achieving 4.2% organic sales growth this quarter, ahead of the total CPG category's 2.1% per IRI data, while expanding underlying operating margins by 110 basis points to 18.4%.

On portfolio optimization, we're sharpening focus on high-velocity, high-margin power brands, now 82% of our North American portfolio, up from 75% last year. This involved divesting a low-growth legacy snacks business to a private equity firm for $450 million, which we're reinvesting in better opportunities. In personal care, our Lumina Shampoo line added 1.3 share points per IRI, hitting 14.2% household penetration through targeted trade and shopper marketing. In EMEA, our focus-and-simplify approach kept organic growth flat against a -1.5% category decline, with share steady at 11.8% via Kantar. We've unlocked $180 million in annualized productivity from SKU rationalization, cutting count by 15% without losing velocity.

Innovation and premiumization are capturing consumers trading up, as premium segments grew 7% per Nielsen versus 1% mass. We launched 12 new SKUs, like our plant-based VitalBev kombucha, ramping to $25 million in sales, 30% ahead of plan, driven by Gen Z in functional beverages—similar to PepsiCo's Poppi or Keurig Dr Pepper's AHA. In household care, PureShield wipes gained 250 bps share in APAC, targeting 15% CAGR in premium cleaners through FY25. Premium products now fuel 35% of topline, up 500 bps year-over-year, adding 2.5 points to organic growth. R&D at 2.8% of sales supports 80 projects in testing.

Sustainability leadership is a true growth driver. Our Planet Positive goals—net-zero Scope 1 and 2 by 2035, 50% recycled packaging by 2028—appeal to 68% of millennials per our insights. We've hit 42% recyclable or compostable packaging, ahead of 40%, with rPET rollout for AquaPure water in LATAM cutting virgin plastic 28%. 95% palm oil is RSPO-certified, on pace for 100% by year-end. This boosted European brand favorability 12%, aiding premium pricing of $120 million year-to-date at 8-10% green premiums.

Digital acceleration has e-commerce at 22% of North American sales, up from 18%, beating category 16% per Circana. Our $150 million Shopper 360 platform uses AI personalization like Amazon's, with DTC up 45%, app at 4.2 million monthly active users and 28% repeat rate. In China, Tmall and JD.com partnerships hit 18% e-comm penetration, adding 400 bps beauty share. Blockchain traces 70% ingredients, cutting stockouts 22% and lifting forecast accuracy to 92%, building to $1 billion digital revenue by FY26.

These priorities set us for 3-5% organic growth and 100-150 bps margin expansion in FY24, with 85% FX hedging, asset-light model, and 95% free cash flow conversion.

I will now turn the call over to Jordan Lee to provide more detail on our financial results.

Jordan Lee:  
Thank you, Alex. As Alex mentioned, we delivered a solid quarter. Net sales were $14.7 billion, representing a 4.8% increase compared to the prior year, or 4.1% organic excluding FX and acquisitions. This marks our third consecutive quarter of organic growth acceleration, outpacing the global CPG industry average of 2.5% per NielsenIQ. Gross margin was 48.2%, up 210 basis points, driven by supply chain efficiencies from our $250 million Resilient Ops initiative—including AI demand forecasting with Palantir, cutting inventory 12% and stockouts 40%, plus hedging 85% of 2024 input costs. Operating income was $2.9 billion, up 7.2%, with EBITDA margins at 19.8%, up 110 bps, thanks to optimized A&P at 10.2% of sales versus 11.1%, shifting to retail media like Walmart Connect for 25% ROAS uplift. Diluted earnings per share were $1.32 adjusted, up 9.5%, with free cash flow of $1.8 billion supporting $800 million share repurchases and a 12% dividend increase to $0.78—our 28th straight hike. ROIC is 18.4%, above our 15% WACC.

The CPG sector faced headwinds from 6-8% input inflation in cocoa, palm oil, and PET, plus softening value channel demand. Yet our Power Brands First strategy balanced pricing, volume recovery, and margins. Volume grew 1.3%, strongest in six quarters, via share gains in high-velocity categories; price/mix added 2.8% from premium SKUs and health & wellness mix now 28% of portfolio, up from 24%.

By segment: Food & Beverage at $7.2 billion, +5.6% organic, led by OatFlex plant-based milks gaining 3.2 points North America share per IRI. Health & Personal Care $4.9 billion, +3.9% organic, e-commerce at 22% up 30%. Household & Beauty Essentials $2.6 billion, +2.7% organic, SKU pruning 15% low-margin for eco-concentrates.

Regionally: North America 55% mix, +6.1% organic on premium health like VitalFit at 4.1% ACV echoing Nestlé's Core Power, club strength at Costco. EMEA 25%, 2.4% amid 9% energy inflation, gains in Turkish Delight and UK eco-lines. APAC +7.2%, China skincare and India snacks like PepsiCo Lay's, e-comm 35%. LATAM +3.8% despite FX.

Strategically, 12 FY25 launches like zero-sugar PureBrew RTDs for Gen Z TikTok; $1.2B IndieBeauty Labs acquisition EPS-accretive; Scope 3 emissions down 18% via regenerative ag.

Now, turning to market share trends, we gained a net 110 bps globally in value share to 14.2% per Nielsen, IRI, Kantar—sixth straight quarter. Snacks +180 bps to 22.5%, CrunchMax and FiberFit leading better-for-you at 35% U.S. $12B share ahead of PepsiCo, Mondelēz; ASP +7% via merchandising, DTC. Beverages value flat 13.8%, volume +60 bps to 12.4%; CSD +40 bps to 18.2%, non-carb VitaQuench +250 bps to 9.7% hydration; energy -30 bps to 8.5% but zero-sugar waters gaining. Personal Care value -20 bps to 11.6%, but premium skincare/hair +140 bps to 16.8%, GlowEssence 12.4% anti-aging. Household +90 bps to 15.3%, disinfectants +120 bps to 21.1% EcoShield.

By region: North America +140 bps to 18.7%, snacks/beverages +250 bps U.S. ACV 28.4%, e-comm 22%. Europe +80 bps to 12.9%, EcoShield 19% Germany eco-detergents. APAC +220 bps to 10.4%, China snacks +300 bps 14.2%, India beverages +180 bps. LATAM +160 bps to 9.8%, Brazil household +200 bps. Rest +100 bps Middle East.

Driven by Category Acceleration Playbook: 15% R&D ($450M) 20 SKUs AI flavors; 50k ACV QSRs Yum! +12% velocity; 65% recyclable portfolio +8 loyalty; dynamic pricing. Expect 80-100 bps FY24 gains.

On organic sales decomposition, total net sales $14.7 billion up 4.8%, organic 4.1%—third mid-single-digit quarter beating 2.1% industry, +110 bps share. Volume +1.3%, price +1.5% moderated from lapping inflation via EDLP, mix +1.1% premiumization.

Segments: Food & Snacks +6.2% (vol +3.5% VitalSnax +12% HHP 92% ACV +80 bps vs Kellogg; price -0.2%; mix +2.9% premium 28%). Beverages +5.1% (vol +1.8% PureFlow +8% e-comm; price +2.4% +15% costs AI elasticity -0.6x; mix +0.9% functional 35%). Household +3.9% (vol +0.8% EcoClean +1.2 pts; price +2.1% 4-6% list; mix +1.0% refill). Personal Care +2.8% (vol -0.5%; price +1.3%; mix +1.9% premium 42%).

Regions: NA +5.4% (vol +3.2% Walmart/Kroger DTC; price +1.0%; mix +1.2%). Europe +3.2% (vol +0.4%; price +2.5%; mix +0.3%). EM +5.1% (vol +1.9%; price +1.6%; mix +1.6% Brazil/India).

Growth Accelerator $250M RGM tech prunes low SKUs $80M savings; Power Brands 65% sales 2x growth; sustainability +22% vol EcoClean. Q4 4-5% organic vol +2.5%.

For capex, FY24 $1.25B up 12%, 45% manufacturing $560M: Vietnam $200M skincare plant 20% vol ASEAN; NA $150M Ohio/Texas automation +25% throughput -15% labor P&G-style. Regional: NA 35%, Europe 25% Poland oat milk, EM 40% Mexico. Supply chain $310M: Reno DC AS/RS e-comm, cold chain $90M, Netherlands $50M -10-15% costs DIO 38 days. Sustainability $250M: solar $100M 25% US energy, rPET $80M -40% plastic, water $40M 80% recycle, pouches $30M. Digital $130M AI OEE +5pts, 5G blockchain RSPO.

FY25 $1.3-1.4B APAC bias, 2.5-3yr payback 200bps margin.

Gross margin 48.2% +210bps: premium mix, $250M productivity AI Blue Yonder -22% obsolescence, nearshoring -18% freight, ag pilots 5-7% inputs. FY24 48.0-48.5% +150bps Q4 48.5-49.0%; pricing +120bps 3-4% AUR, productivity +140bps, mix +20bps. Headwinds commodity -90bps cocoa $7500 hedged, FX -20bps. Regional NA 49%, Europe 47.5%, EM 45%, ROW.

Margin Momentum 50% cost 30% price/mix 20% innovation; divest $150M fund adjacencies.

We continue to manage costs effectively and invest in growth. Next, I will turn the call over to Taylor Kim to discuss marketing and brand performance.

Taylor Kim:  
Thank you, Jordan. We saw strong performance in our core brands, particularly VitalFit. Our digital marketing efforts are driving significant engagement, and we are seeing strong results from our Healthy Horizons campaign. Our brands are gaining traction through targeted shopper insights and omnichannel strategies, aligning with consumer shifts to health and sustainability. We've optimized media toward high-ROAS channels, supporting the share gains Jordan outlined.

Following me, Morgan Patel will provide an update on our supply chain initiatives.

Morgan Patel:  
Thank you, Taylor. We continue to focus on optimizing our supply chain to improve efficiency and reduce costs. We are implementing new technologies and processes to enhance our responsiveness to changing market conditions, including AI forecasting and nearshoring that contributed to margin gains. We are also actively working to mitigate the impact of supply chain disruptions through hedging, automation, and resilient logistics networks.

Operator, we are now ready to open the call for questions.

Operator:  
Thank you. Instructions for participating in the question-and-answer session will be given momentarily. Our first question comes from Mike Johnson with Goldman Sachs.

Mike Johnson:  
Could you provide more insight into the geographic performance, particularly in emerging markets?

Alex Rivera:  
Thanks, Mike. Geographically, North America led with 6.1% organic growth on premium health and club channels. EMEA was 2.4% amid energy costs but gained on eco-products. APAC surged 7.2%, with China skincare recovery and India snacks expansion via e-comm at 35% on Tmall and Flipkart. LATAM held 3.8% despite FX, through localized pricing. Emerging markets drove outsized share gains, like +220 bps in APAC to 10.4%, with Brazil household +200 bps. Our playbook prioritizes urbanization and premium there.

Operator:  
Our next question comes from Lisa Chen with JPMorgan.

Lisa Chen:  
How are you managing inventory levels given the current economic uncertainty?

Jordan Lee:  
Good question, Lisa. Our Resilient Ops initiative with Palantir AI reduced inventory 12% while cutting stockouts 40%, DIO targeting 38 days via capex in DCs like Reno AS/RS. Nearshoring and hedging 85% inputs buffer volatility. Amid uncertainty, we're balancing volume recovery with efficiency, maintaining 98% in-stock versus industry 92%, supporting share gains without excess.

Operator:  
Our next question comes from David Patel with Morgan Stanley.

David Patel:  
Can you discuss the progress on your sustainability goals and any related cost implications?

Morgan Patel:  
Absolutely, David. Sustainability is embedded in our strategy—42% packaging recyclable ahead of target, rPET cutting virgin plastic 28%, 95% RSPO palm oil. Scope 3 down 18% via regenerative ag. Capex $250M for solar, water recycling 80%, mono-pouches. Costs? Green premiums added $120M pricing power, loyalty +8 points, ROAS uplift—net positive, ahead of peers like Colgate.

Operator:  
Our next question comes from Emily Rodriguez with Barclays.

Emily Rodriguez:  
What are your expectations for pricing elasticity in the coming quarters?

Taylor Kim:  
Thanks, Emily. Elasticity remains resilient at around -0.6x, per our AI models. Q4 pricing 3-4% targeted on elastic categories like snacks and CSDs via EDLP and value packs, lapping prior pass-throughs. Premium mix and innovations like zero-sugar drive uptake without volume drag, as seen in +1.5% price contribution. We'll monitor consumer value-seeking but expect sustained discipline.

Operator:  
There are no further questions at this time. I will now turn the call back to Alex Rivera for closing remarks.

Alex Rivera:  
Thank you, Operator, and thank you all for your insightful questions. We remain committed to delivering strong results and creating value for our shareholders—FY24 organic 4-5%, EPS 8-10%. We look forward to updating you on our progress next quarter.

Sarah Thompson:  
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the Vitality Consumer Goods Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. You may now disconnect.
